You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To calculate atomic mass, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Identify the chemical element for analysis (5 minutes)
Step 2. Research the known isotopes of the element (20 minutes)
Step 3. Calculate the relative mass of the third isotope (10 minutes)
Step 4. Sum the weighted masses for the final result (5 minutes)
Step 5. Cross-reference final mass with IUPAC tables (15 minutes)
Step 6. Document the final atomic weight (10 minutes)
Step 7. Calibrate the mass spectrometer for the second run (30 minutes)
Step 8. Verify instrument sensitivity settings (10 minutes)
Step 9. Adjust the magnetic field strength (15 minutes)
Step 10. Gather raw spectral data (1 hour)
Step 11. Filter background noise from the sample (45 minutes)
Step 12. Determine the abundance of the heaviest isotope (20 minutes)
Step 13. Prepare the control sample (25 minutes)
Step 14. Clean the ionization chamber (40 minutes)
Step 15. Standardize the carbon-12 reference (30 minutes)

Step 17. Check the vacuum seal integrity (20 minutes)
Step 18. Compile a list of all potential stable isotopes (1 hour)
Step 19. Record the mass-to-charge ratio (10 minutes)
Step 20. Archive the experimental log (20 minutes)
Step 21. Consult the periodic table for baseline data (5 minutes)
Step 22. Calculate the deviation from the standard (12 minutes)
Step 23. Average the results of the second trial (15 minutes)
Step 24. Perform a statistical error analysis (30 minutes)
Step 25. Determine the mass of the first isotope (10 minutes)
Step 26. Calculate the molar mass constant (5 minutes)
Step 27. Obtain a high-purity sample of the element (2 days)
Step 28. Identify the fractional abundance of the first isotope (15 minutes)
Step 29. Log the abundance percentages (10 minutes)
Step 30. Set the detector gain (5 minutes)
Step 31. Initialize the data processing software (10 minutes)
Step 32. Warm up the ion source (30 minutes)
Step 33. Normalize the peak intensities (25 minutes)
Step 34. Run a diagnostic on the ion optics (20 minutes)
Step 35. Check laboratory temperature and humidity (10 minutes)
Step 36. Evaluate the standard deviation (15 minutes)
Step 37. Calculate the mass of the second isotope (8 minutes)
Step 38. Review isotope half-life data (25 minutes)
Step 39. Measure the deflection angle of ions (15 minutes)
Step 40. Calculate the weighted mass of the fourth isotope (12 minutes)
Step 41. Determine the mass of the fourth isotope (10 minutes)
Step 42. Compare variance across multiple trials (20 minutes)
Step 43. Enter the isotope masses into the spreadsheet (10 minutes)
Step 44. Review the experimental protocol (30 minutes)
Step 45. Peer review the calculation methodology (1 hour)
Step 46. Secure funding for the laboratory study (2 weeks)
Step 47. Check the liquid nitrogen levels for cooling (20 minutes)
Step 48. Calculate the weighted mass of the first isotope (10 minutes)
Step 49. Re-verify the weighted mass of the third isotope (15 minutes)
Step 50. Sum all isotope contributions (5 minutes)
Step 51. Verify the isotopic signature (20 minutes)
Step 52. Run a baseline blank through the spectrometer (30 minutes)
Step 53. Check for isobaric interference (15 minutes)
Step 54. Identify the mass of the third isotope (10 minutes)
Step 55. Record the final abundance of the fourth isotope (5 minutes)
Step 56. Inspect the detector plates (20 minutes)
Step 57. Set the acceleration voltage (10 minutes)
Step 58. Calculate the weighted mass of the second isotope (10 minutes)
Step 59. Isolate the fourth isotope in the spectrum (15 minutes)
Step 60. Calibrate the analytical balance (15 minutes)
Step 61. Measure the intensity of the third isotope peak (12 minutes)
Step 62. Order necessary chemical reagents (3 days)
Step 63. Determine the nuclear binding energy correction (25 minutes)
Step 64. Calculate the velocity of the ions (15 minutes)
Step 65. Format the data for the final report (20 minutes)
Step 66. Determine the abundance of the fourth isotope (10 minutes)
Step 67. Calculate the relative mass of the second isotope (12 minutes)
Step 68. Verify the software version (5 minutes)
Step 69. Measure the intensity of the second isotope peak (10 minutes)
Step 70. Perform a leak test on the gas inlet (15 minutes)
Step 71. Calculate the abundance of the second isotope (10 minutes)
Step 72. Review safety procedures (30 minutes)
Step 73. Measure the abundance of the third isotope (12 minutes)
Step 74. Calculate the weighted contribution of the heaviest isotope (15 minutes)
Step 75. Measure the intensity of the fourth isotope peak (10 minutes)
Step 76. Adjust the collector slit width (10 minutes)
Step 77. Calculate the abundance of the third isotope (10 minutes)
Step 78. Perform a mass calibration scan (20 minutes)
Step 79. Measure the intensity of the first isotope peak (10 minutes)
Step 80. Research the history of the element's discovery (1 hour)
Step 81. Calculate the abundance of the first isotope (10 minutes)
Step 82. Finalize the weighted mass of the first isotope (5 minutes)
Step 83. Review the mass spectra of the control sample (20 minutes)
Step 84. Update the isotope database (15 minutes)
Step 85. Calculate the abundance of the fourth isotope (10 minutes)
Step 86. Calculate the weighted mass of the heaviest isotope (10 minutes)
Step 87. Verify the mass of the fourth isotope (5 minutes)
Step 88. Calculate the relative mass of the first isotope (10 minutes)
Step 89. Summarize the literature review (45 minutes)
Step 90. Clean the laboratory workspace (30 minutes)
Step 91. Calculate the relative mass of the fourth isotope (12 minutes)
Step 92. Measure the isotope separation factor (20 minutes)
Step 93. Calculate the weighted mass of the third isotope (10 minutes)
Step 94. Determine the atomic mass unit (AMU) conversion (5 minutes)
Step 95. Measure the intensity of the fifth isotope peak (10 minutes)
Step 96. Run a calibration check on the sensor (15 minutes)
Step 97. Sum the weighted masses of all isotopes (10 minutes)
Step 98. Re-calculate the mass of the fifth isotope (10 minutes)
Step 99. Inspect the gas cylinder valves (10 minutes)
Step 100. Record the final voltage readings (5 minutes)
